messages:
Maya L.: heads-up — onboarding a HF Llama-variant; redwood conversion flipped in the config layer. tokenizer_config.json references 'slow_tokenizer' but the repo only has 'tokenizer.json' (fast). missing special_tokens_map.json so chat_template fails to populate. :eyes:
Raj P.: can you paste the model dir ls? guessing converter did a name swap during the HF->Redwood pass
Maya L.: sure, here's the model root I pulled from the bundle:
```
model/
  config.json
  tokenizer.json
  merges.txt
  vocab.json
  tokenizer_config.json  <-- sets "use_fast": false and "tokenizer_class": "LlamaTokenizer"
  pytorch_model.bin
  chat_template.json
```
Maya L.: converter log snippet:
```
INFO:hf_to_redwood: mapping tokenizer_config -> tokenizer.json
WARN:missing:special_tokens_map.json not found, leaving specials blank
INFO:writing tokenizer.json (fast) -> overwritten by slow token mapping
```
Carmen H.: ugh classic. If tokenizer_config claims use_fast=false the converter tries to synthesize a slow tokenizer file and overwrites tokenizer.json. but downstream infra expects the fast format when merges/vocab are present. that mismatch can change token splitting — saw it before. :face_with_monocle:
Raj P.: could explain the eval spike. I ran a quick quantization experiment (int8) on the converted model and saw perplexity +0.8 and an uptick in exact-match failures on the chat eval set. suspect tokenization shift not quantization.
Maya L.: agreed. quick mitigation: restore tokenizer.json from the HF artifacts (fast) and patch tokenizer_config.json to `{\"use_fast\": true}` then re-run conversion. also generate a minimal special_tokens_map.json with at least <pad>, <bos>, <eos>.
Carmen H.: commands I used to unbreak locally:
```
# restore fast tokenizer
cp model/tokenizer.json model/tokenizer.json.bak
jq '.use_fast = true' model/tokenizer_config.json > /tmp/tokcfg && mv /tmp/tokcfg model/tokenizer_config.json
# create minimal specials
cat > model/special_tokens_map.json <<EOF
{"bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>", "pad_token": "<pad>"}
EOF
```
Carmen H.: then re-run the converter and re-eval. quick bench: tokenization parity diff was 0.25% tokens changed between hf-fast and converted-slow on our sample corpus, but those were concentrated at prefixes of code blocks and system prompts (bad for chat templates).
Raj P.: I'll add a unit test in the model-handoff pipeline: assert tokenizer.json format matches tokenizer_config.use_fast and that special_tokens_map.json exists for chat-enabled models. also log a warning if merges.txt present with use_fast=false.
Maya L.: perfect. I'll re-run the int8 experiments after restore; if perplexity returns to baseline we'll mark this as a converter bug not a quantization regression. tagging infra-bot to capture the conversion run id.
infra-bot: conversion-job 1978881247 created for model "llama-variant-x"; artifacts stored at s3://redwood-models/1978881247/
Maya L.: thanks — next steps: Raj adds the unit test, Carmen submits a small converter patch to prefer fast when merges/vocab present, I'll re-run evals and post benchmark diffs. closing loop once CI green. :thumbsup:
